messages:
alice: Heads-up — customer asked if we can keep BYOK telemetry (usage metrics, op metadata) for 7 years for a financial regulator. They explicitly said no access to key material. Can we map this to our current audit retention & RBAC?
maria: short answer: yes for telemetry, but needs careful scoping. we must ensure KMS/HSM material never leaves custody. telemetry should be event metadata only (:timestamp, operation, principal, resource id, result).
sam: what counts as 'telemetry' vs 'sensitive metadata'? e.g. API call args might include model prompts with PII.
ajake: agree — telemetry = operational fields only. anything in request/response bodies is data plane and subject to data-retention rules. need a sanitizer pipeline before logs persist.
maria: we should propose: (1) RBAC change to create a "telemetry-reader" role with access to audit indices but blocked from keystore endpoints; (2) ingest pipeline to scrub request/response payloads before indexing; (3) legal attestation that we never log key material or unredacted customer data.
sec-bot: AUTOMATION: created ticket INF-4821 to add telemetry-reader role; assigned to @maria.
alice: for RBAC specifics — can we do attribute-based restrictions on the KMS proxies? like deny any read when request path contains /key-material or CEK?
maria: KMS proxy supports path-based allow/deny and mTLS client cert mapping today. we can add an explicit deny rule: `deny if request.path matches \/keystore\/v1\/keys\/.*\/material` and `allow if principal in telemetry-role for /audit/*`
alice: can you paste a minimal policy snippet?
maria: sure:
```json
{
  "Version": "2023-07-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Deny", "Action": "kms:GetKeyMaterial", "Resource": "arn:redwood:kms:customer:*:key/*"},
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["audit:ReadEvents"], "Resource": "arn:redwood:audit:customer:*:log/*", "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"redwood:Role": "telemetry-reader"}}}
  ]
}
```
jake: also need to update keystore proxy logging so it never emits `key_blob` or `plaintext_key` fields. transform stage must drop those before the audit sink.
legal: regulator typically wants an attestation + retention schedule. 7 years is long; we need to ensure we don't accidentally retain PII. extract: store only `operation`, `status`, `principal_id`, `resource_hash`, `timestamp`. resource_hash can be HMAC of resource id using operator-only key so we can correlate without storing the raw id.
sam: HMAC idea is good. who holds the HMAC key? cannot be customer keys. should be service-side key in HSM with operator-only ACLs and rotate quarterly.
maria: ops note: add rewrap/rotation step to SOP. if using HMAC, include `hmac_salt_version` in logs for future verification.
alice: incident scenario: if an exfil attempt happens, compliance may request key access logs. we must show timeline but not key material. confirm that our current audit query can produce: [timeline with hashed resource, principal, action, result, node id].
ajake: yes — Kibana dashboard can produce that. need one small change: index mapping must include `resource_hash` and `hmac_salt_version` as keywords. will file mapping change in INF-4822.
sec-bot: AUTOMATION: created ticket INF-4822 for index mapping changes; assigned to @jake.
alice: vuln triage angle — if a compromised operator account exists, could they infer key ids from telemetry? hashed ids could be brute-forced if salt leaked. mitigation: per-customer salt + pepper stored in KMS HSM with strict ACLs.
maria: add rate-limiting on hash-lookup APIs and monitor suspicious query patterns. also limit telemetry-reader to specific organizational units (scoped by customer).
legal: add clause to customer contract: we retain operational telemetry for X years; never store key material; we will provide attestation and audit logs on request. also need Data Processing Agreement updates for long retention.
sam: timeline: can we deliver RBAC + scrub pipeline + mapping change in 2 sprints?
maria: sprint plan: sprint A — RBAC role + proxy deny rule + ticket INF-4821; sprint B — scrub pipeline + index mapping INF-4822 + HMAC key provisioning and rotation.
ajake: QA: simulate a request and ensure scrub removes payloads. here's a sample log lines BEFORE -> AFTER: 
BEFORE: `{ "timestamp":"...","operation":"Encrypt","principal":"op-123","request":{"key_id":"cust-key-9","key_blob":"BASE64...","plaintext":"..."}}`
AFTER: `{ "timestamp":"...","operation":"Encrypt","principal":"op-123","resource_hash":"h1xx3f..","result":"OK","hmac_salt_version":"v2"}`
sec-bot: NOTE: compliance checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/compliance/byok-telemetry (draft)
alice: ok good. last question — for on-call incident response, do we permit temporary elevation to view raw audit payloads if there's a live incident? what's the approval flow?
maria: approvals: require 2-person approval from security lead + legal; create timebound ephemeral credential with one-hour TTL; operations must record reason and get automated Slack approval flow.
legal: also require post-incident attestation and redaction review before any raw artifacts are shared externally.
sam: i'll draft the ephemeral elevation play in INF-4823.
sec-bot: AUTOMATION: created ticket INF-4823 for ephemeral elevation workflow; assigned to @sam.
alice: thanks everyone. i'll reply to the customer with this approach and ask for exact retention start date and any specific fields they require. :thumbsup:
